guardrails.title: Own and reconcile each Paper BossBar audience explicitly
rules: Give each logical BossBar slot exactly one plugin-owned current generation. Keep the bar handle, candidate state, winner, desired viewer identities, applied viewer identities, writer, and cleanup state under that owner.

Compute viewer eligibility before selection from explicit gates such as active owner state, current player session and backend, plugin admission, permission, world, distance, visibility, or other stated product rules. A stable identity match alone is not eligibility.

When several candidates compete for one logical slot, rank them by declared priority and a stable tie-break key, then apply explicit hysteresis such as an enter threshold, exit threshold, minimum hold, or switch margin using a monotonic clock. Apply this one-winner policy only to that declared slot, and keep independent slots when multiple simultaneous bars are intentional.

Treat a freshly computed desired viewer identity set as authoritative. In the verified Paper execution context, snapshot current viewers, remove current-minus-desired viewers, then add desired-minus-current viewers after rechecking their current session and eligibility.

Do not retain Player objects in candidate, desired, applied, queued, or durable state. Resolve live Player objects only while applying one reconciliation or terminal cleanup in the required execution context.

Route every BossBar mutation through one serialized writer for the logical slot. Each accepted command carries the owner generation and a strictly increasing slot revision, and the writer rejects a stale generation, an older or duplicate revision, and publication after terminal state.

Bound and observe pending updates per logical slot and across the manager. Coalesce replaceable title, progress, style, winner, and viewer-set updates by slot and revision, while ensuring overload cannot discard or indefinitely delay terminal hide and removal.

On replacement, terminally hide and detach the old generation before publishing the new bar. If detachment cannot be confirmed within the cleanup budget, reject or defer replacement with an observable failure instead of silently overlapping generations. A late callback from the old generation must not attach viewers, change the winner, or mutate the replacement.

Route owner completion, feature or encounter end, an owning player-session close, reconnect or relevant backend transfer, plugin disable or reload, replacement, partial initialization failure, repeated signals, and orphan-owner reconciliation through one idempotent terminal transition. A non-owning viewer-session end removes only that viewer through eligibility reconciliation instead of closing a shared bar.

Terminal cleanup closes update admission, hides the bar with a target-version-verified visibility member, removes every attached player, and clears desired and applied viewer identities plus reverse indexes. Keep the generation terminal when one action fails, continue independent cleanup, and release the last bar handle only after detachment is confirmed or a bounded observable cleanup-failure outcome is recorded. Never retain Player objects for retry. Verify any registered-bar removal API separately before using it.

Run bounded reconciliation for orphaned owners and viewer drift, and observe active generations, queued revisions, winner switches, suppressed switches, viewer add/remove balance, rejected stale updates, terminal reasons, and nonzero viewers after close.

Verify target-version BossBar type and member behavior in official Paper Javadocs. API members that add, remove, list, hide, or detach viewers do not by themselves prove plugin ownership, stable arbitration, lifecycle coverage, thread safety, or distributed handoff.

For reconnect or backend transfer of a session-owned bar, create a fresh local generation and define an explicit plugin-owned handoff or fencing policy when state crosses servers. For a shared owner, invalidate only the departing viewer unless the owner itself ends. Do not claim that Paper BossBar APIs provide distributed ownership or clean a previous backend automatically.

Test rapid enter and leave around thresholds, deterministic replacement, reconnect and backend transfer, repeated disable cleanup, stale generations and revisions, bounded-queue overload, missing lifecycle signals, and zero viewer or reverse-index leaks after every terminal path.

Keep boss AI, combat or encounter mechanics, custom mob systems, ModelEngine integration, scoreboard or action-bar policy, and vanilla /bossbar command authoring outside this BossBar audience-lifecycle concern.

For side effects that cannot be atomically swapped or rolled back, define ordered compensation, degraded state, observability, and operator recovery instead of reporting unconditional success.
Consumers must capture one immutable snapshot or verify configuration generation and plugin epoch before publishing; mutable configuration objects must not be shared as live cross-thread state.
Reject restart-only changes before commit and expose them as a typed restart-required result rather than silently leaving file and effective state different.

Do not save stale cached configuration over an externally edited file; use known-revision writes and safe replacement through the same validation path, or keep generated state in a separately owned store.
Cancel reload admission during disable and close prepared, live, and retired resources idempotently even when individual cleanup actions fail.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper persistent data typed, owned, versioned, and recoverable
rules: Create reusable NamespacedKey values in the owning plugin namespace; use another namespace only through an explicit cross-plugin contract.
Maintain a closed data dictionary for every key: holder scope, primitive PersistentDataType, complex representation, optionality, default, bounds, schema version, readers, and writers.
Treat has(key) as existence only and has(key, type) as primitive-type matching only. A custom adapter backed by BYTE_ARRAY does not make an arbitrary byte array a valid complex value.
Handle missing, wrong-primitive, malformed, oversized, unknown-value, supported-old, and unsupported-future data as distinct typed outcomes.
Bound byte arrays, numeric arrays, strings, lists, nested tag containers, nesting depth, and all allocations before domain publication.

Choose a PersistentDataHolder whose lifecycle matches the record, and verify the target-version read and mutation-publication path instead of retaining detached snapshots or temporary edit containers.

Use read-only views for inspection, treat OfflinePlayer PDC as read-only where documented, publish TileState snapshot changes with the required update, and verify version-gated ItemStack access before use.
Never assume PDC copies when data moves between holders. Define selected keys, destination collision behavior, source deletion, retries, and recovery explicitly.
Use copyTo only when copying every custom key is intended and choose replace deliberately; otherwise copy an allowlist of owned keys and preserve foreign namespaces.
Use remove for deletion because set rejects null, and do not clear or rewrite keys outside the plugin's ownership contract.

Version each independently evolved record; validate all migration steps before publishing the new state and advancing its marker, preserve or reject unsupported-future data, and make retries idempotent.
Use a nested tag container or an explicit recovery protocol when multiple fields must change together; do not describe PDC as transactional.
Do not infer save timing, thread safety, or scheduler compatibility from PDC type or member indexes; verify holder behavior and access context for the target Paper version.
Test codecs and migrations purely, then use a loaded target-version Paper server for holder snapshot, update, serialization, unload, reload, or restart behavior that the claim requires.
Keep ItemStack logical identity, similarity, and presentation ownership outside this generic storage contract.
requiredEvidence: target-version Paper type/member matches plus official PDC guide and Javadocs behavior for every holder and PDC operation referenced
a key/type/bounds/schema ownership registry and holder-lifetime publication table
a bounded migration, copy, replace, removal, and recovery design that preserves foreign and unsupported-future data
wrong-type, malformed, oversized, old-version, future-version, repeated-migration, copy-collision, holder-boundary, and restart tests at sufficient evidence layers
guardrails.failureMode: A PDC value can be present but unreadable, semantically malformed, attached to the wrong lifetime, partially migrated, unintentionally copied or deleted, or falsely reported durable without target-version runtime evidence.

guardrails.title: Keep server-backed Minecraft UI pages bounded, ordered, and generation-safe
rules: Fetch one bounded page at the database, repository, or service boundary; never fetch all matching rows and slice or truncate them in plugin or client memory.
Give each record a stable ID and define a total deterministic order with a unique tie-breaker plus explicit null and collation behavior.
Keep opaque cursors server-owned and bind them to viewer authorization, filters, search, sort, direction, and any snapshot or revision they require.
An opaque cursor is not itself a snapshot guarantee; state whether the feed is snapshot-consistent or live and document the insertion and deletion behavior actually provided.
Return bounded items, nextCursor or equivalent continuation, explicit exhausted semantics, current request generation or correlation, and the accepted revision when the consistency contract uses one.
Distinguish initial loading, ready, loading more, empty, error, retrying, reset, and exhausted states.
Accept a response only for the current viewer generation, query, direction, expected predecessor cursor, correlation, and revision.

Handle duplicate page delivery idempotently and deduplicate rows by stable item ID without reordering; if the same ID has changed payload, reject it under snapshot semantics or use an explicit monotonic version and replace rule under live-feed semantics instead of silently choosing first or last, and reposition or reset if a sort field changed.
Reject reversed, skipped, out-of-order, cyclic, nonadvancing, and late pages.
Start a fresh generation on filter, search, sort, authorization, reconnect, or viewer-instance changes; reopen resumes only through an intentionally validated token.
When data shrinks, reset or refresh a cursor view, or clamp a numbered view against refreshed snapshot totals; never loop on the same empty out-of-range page.
Bound page size, lookahead, in-flight requests, queued pages, retained rows, retries, and prefetch distance, and stop prefetch at failure or explicit exhaustion.
Reauthorize every page request at the server boundary instead of treating a prior page or cursor as lasting permission.

Test empty and exact page boundaries, tied sort values, insertions, deletions, final-page shrink, identical, changed non-sort, and changed sort payload duplicates for one stable ID, reversed and stale completion, query reset, reopen, reconnect, cursor rejection and cycles, retry, and prefetch bounds.

Route inventory click and settlement, protocol framing and hostile decoding, connection teardown, and runtime evidence to their dedicated guidance; keep rendering geometry, screen-specific design, persistence flush, and business-specific page sizes outside this concern.

Repository, query, or adapter evidence that each request retrieves only one bounded page plus bounded lookahead or count work
Request, response, and UI-state definitions covering generation, query, nextCursor or equivalent continuation, items, exhausted, loading, empty, failure, reset, and terminal states
Acceptance and reset logic for duplicate, reversed, out-of-order, nonadvancing, cyclic, late, reopened, reconnected, changed-query, and stale-revision responses
Deterministic boundary and mutation tests plus adapter-level proof of source paging and explicit request, memory, retry, and prefetch bounds
guardrails.failureMode: A list that only looks paged can silently omit records, load the complete collection, skip ties, duplicate or reverse pages, append stale results to a replacement viewer, or run unbounded requests and memory after data changes.

guardrails.title: Preserve foreign scoreboard ownership across sidebar lifecycle changes
rules: Verify every scoreboard type, member, event candidate, display behavior, identifier bound, text bound, and visible-row bound against the exact target Paper and client version; do not reuse numeric constants or lifecycle assumptions from another release.

Give each viewer one explicit scoreboard owner containing viewer-session, plugin, owner, and update generations, the installed scoreboard identity, exact prior scoreboard, restore policy, desired and applied revisions, and close state.

Require each installed board to be private to one viewer, or model a separate shared-board group generation with a membership ledger or reference count, one compatible desired and applied snapshot, and a registration ledger; reject or isolate viewer-specific content, and never let one viewer's close unregister content still displayed by another member.
Capture the prior scoreboard only before first installation; rapid replacement must invalidate the old generation and carry the original prior board forward.
Restore only when the live viewer still belongs to the current generation and still displays the exact scoreboard installed by that owner; preserve any foreign replacement.
Represent restored, foreign-superseded, viewer-unavailable, and restoration-failed outcomes explicitly, and recheck ownership before any documented fallback.

Treat revoked feature eligibility as a hide trigger while requiring the same API-valid live viewer session for restoration; do not require the feature to remain eligible before restoring its prior scoreboard.
Derive stable bounded objective, team, and entry identifiers, look before registration, and reuse or unregister a same-name object only when a ledger proves the same owner and schema.
Never broadly reset, unregister, or mutate registrations on a prior, shared, or foreign scoreboard; clean only entries recorded by the active owner.
Separate unique entry identity from display text so duplicate labels remain valid without registration collisions.
Build immutable desired snapshots with stable logical line IDs and a total deterministic presentation key; preserve tied business ranks as data but use a unique verified presentation order.
Apply target-version bounds before mutation and return an explicit visible subset plus omitted result instead of silently clipping or relying on guessed fixed values.
Diff desired against the applied revision, make unchanged publication idempotent, and update only owned stale, changed, or new registrations in a deterministic sequence.
Fence every delayed build, update, and hide with viewer-session, plugin, owner, update, and installed-scoreboard tokens checked immediately before publication; cancellation alone is insufficient.

Use one idempotent close path for mid-session eligibility, join, quit, reconnect, world change, replacement, partial initialization, reload, and disable, without assuming target event order; shared-board membership and registration cleanup wait until that viewer or the final live member no longer displays the board.

Invalidate before cleanup, avoid display mutation after logout, conditionally restore only while still owner, continue only safely independent cleanup after failure, and give any still-displayed owner board an observable bounded retry, quarantine, or terminal-disable outcome instead of claiming all registrations and prior references were released.

Test rapid replacement, old update and hide callbacks, mid-session join, foreign takeover, restoration failure, two viewers sharing and replacing a board, incompatible shared snapshots, duplicate registration, duplicate labels, tied ranks, deterministic ordering, exact and over-limit values, world change, reconnect, reload, and disable.
Keep BossBars, player-name resolution, vanilla command-file authoring, ranking calculation, and business-specific display design outside this concern.

A viewer owner state machine, exact prior-board restore policy, and ledger for objective, team, and entry ownership
A private-board invariant or shared-board group membership and last-member cleanup test
A pure deterministic snapshot and diff contract with explicit ties, truncation, duplicate-label, and idempotency outcomes
Generation-fence and conditional-restore race tests including foreign takeover and restoration failure
A lifecycle matrix and cleanup assertions for mid-session eligibility, join, quit, reconnect, world change, reload, and disable
guardrails.failureMode: A scoreboard owner without identity, generations, bounded registrations, deterministic snapshots, conditional restoration, and complete teardown can overwrite foreign state, publish stale lines, or leak UI resources.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper mob navigation single-owned and recovery bounded
rules: Resolve and document the exact target Paper version before naming Mob, Pathfinder, PathResult, target, pathfinding, removal, or lifecycle APIs.

Represent VANILLA_GOALS, PLUGIN_TARGET, PLUGIN_PATH, and STOPPED as mutually exclusive controller phases; PLUGIN_PATH retains the same target lease and rights from PLUGIN_TARGET rather than creating a second owner.
Identify every plugin controller and request with a stable identity, monotonic generation, bounded lease, eligibility result, deterministic priority and tie-breaker, and typed outcome.
Increment the generation on acquire, preempt, release, reload, and terminal teardown so queued or delayed old work cannot publish.

Immediately before every target or path mutation, verify plugin epoch, controller generation, lease and deadline, mob and target identity, validity, death state, world, and current eligibility in a target-compatible execution context.
Treat a null findPath result as NO_PATH, an insufficient or non-reachable result as PARTIAL_OR_UNREACHABLE, moveTo false as START_REJECTED, and moveTo true as STARTED only.

Treat setTarget and moveTo as intent or start operations, re-observe target and path state in the same verified entity context, and type cancellation, rejection, retargeting, clearing, replacement, and foreign intervention separately.
Prove ARRIVED from current valid entity state within an explicit destination tolerance; moveTo, hasPath, getCurrentPath, path-point exhaustion, and EntityPathfindEvent are not completion signals.
Measure meaningful progress with a stated tolerance and observation window, then distinguish slow progress from STALLED without exact-position or one-tick assumptions.

Keep synchronous Pathfinder calls on the verified entity context, and bound admission, controllers or calculations per pass, minimum replan interval, attempts per lease, backoff, timeout, queue capacity, and per-pass work or CPU budget; terminate or release on exhaustion and never spin every tick.

Give no-path, partial or unreachable, start-rejected, stalled, target-gone, world-change, lease-expired, stale-generation, cancellation, and budget-exhausted outcomes explicit retry, release, or terminal decisions.

Paper exposes no current-path owner token: a matching destination, PathResult, or observable path is not ownership proof. Require an explicit exclusive coordinator or cooperative adapter contract covering all writers before stopping a path, clearing a target, or restoring settings; otherwise fail closed and preserve unknown Paper state.
On hot reload, publish a validated immutable policy generation, reject old results, reconcile controllers within a bound, and keep the last known good generation when the candidate is invalid.

On target loss, world change, mob death or despawn, and disable, close admission, cancel queued work, invalidate generations, and converge repeated cleanup under the writer contract without teleport recovery or new post-disable work.
Prove deterministic ownership and recovery with table-driven tests, and prove referenced Paper navigation and lifecycle semantics on a loaded target-version server.

Keep combat balance, specific mob design, assets, ModelEngine, behavior trees, teleport recovery, broad performance analysis, and generic scheduler, event, configuration, world, and region policy outside this concern.
requiredEvidence: A target-version API and behavior evidence table for Mob, Entity, Pathfinder, PathResult, target events, pathfinding events, and lifecycle observations actually used
A one-owner phase and transition table in which PLUGIN_PATH retains its target lease, with deterministic arbitration, generation changes, and typed acquisition outcomes

A calculation, invocation, observed-post-state, progress, and recovery matrix covering null, partial, unreachable, target cancellation or retargeting, start rejection, foreign intervention, progress, arrival, stall, target loss, world change, expiry, stale completion, cancellation, and budget exhaustion
Explicit arrival and progress tolerances, observation window, replan interval, attempts, backoff, timeout, queue, admission, per-pass, and work budgets on the verified entity context

An exclusive coordinator or cooperative writer contract plus fail-closed evidence proving same-destination and different-destination foreign intervention survives reload, preemption, death, despawn, world change, and disable
Table-driven deterministic tests plus loaded target-version server evidence with exact commands and limitations

guardrails.title: Do not claim more Paper behavior than the completed tests prove
rules: Map every material behavior and final claim to the boundary that can observe it before selecting a test framework.

Treat compilation as type-compatibility evidence only; it does not prove plugin loading, descriptor correctness, dependency wiring, registration, Paper runtime semantics, scheduling, persistence, or client-visible behavior.
Use pure unit tests for deterministic domain rules and plugin-owned contracts, not as substitutes for Bukkit or Paper behavior.

Use mocks and fakes only for caller-controlled interfaces with stated semantics; do not invent return values or lifecycle behavior for undocumented Paper internals and then cite the result as runtime evidence.
Use MockBukkit only for APIs and semantics the selected version of its harness actually supports, and keep unsupported behavior explicit instead of silently stubbing it.

Run a loaded target-version Paper server when changes affect plugin descriptors, bootstrap, dependency injection, command or listener registration, scheduler integration, serialization adapters, reload, or disable behavior.

Use a protocol oracle for packet transport and shape claims; use a real instrumented client or captured client state for rendering, audio, input, resource-pack application, and interaction outcomes that protocol evidence cannot observe.
Control clocks, identifiers, task completion, retries, and timeouts; avoid wall-clock sleeps, live network dependencies, shared mutable fixtures, and test-order coupling.

Cover expected failure outcomes, duplicate and out-of-order callbacks, cancellation, disconnect, partial enable, reload, disable, and stale asynchronous completion whenever those transitions are possible.
Test persistence and migration at the real adapter boundary with isolated temporary state, restart or reload, malformed or older data, and partial-write recovery where applicable.
Restore static state, registries, files, ports, executors, plugin instances, and server fixtures after every test, including failed setup and partial enable.

Report exact commands, target versions, results, known unrelated baselines, skipped checks, unavailable environments, and manual verification still required; scope the conclusion to the strongest completed evidence layer.

target-version unit, harness, loaded-server, or client evidence appropriate to each claim
deterministic lifecycle and asynchronous ordering tests where relevant
exact reproducible test commands and an explicit limitations report

guardrails.title: Keep Fabric Client GameTest visual evidence attributable and reproducible
rules: Freeze a versioned complete case matrix before execution and assign stable semantic case IDs from named dimensions; do not use list position, current time, random values, or artifact filenames as identity.

Record target Minecraft, resolved Fabric stack releases and mappings, test-bundle revision, asset revision, renderer, environment class, viewport, resolved GUI scale, locale, fixture, and visual state metadata needed to decide whether evidence is comparable.

Gate capture on bounded state-specific readiness barriers such as world creation, chunk rendering, asset loading, screen opening, layout completion, and deterministic animation advancement; a fixed sleep is not proof of readiness.

Resolve selected IDs and stable-ID ranges against the frozen suite definition, reject unknown or ambiguous selection, and report expected, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and not-selected sets independently.

Never infer complete-suite success from a selected case, range, shard, resumed subset, or successful process exit. Completeness requires every expected eligible case to have reconciled passing evidence in the declared run set.

Capture and retain a full client frame for each case that reaches successful capture, comparison, or visual pass. When readiness or assertion, render, or capture fails first, record the phase-aware expected absence instead of replacing that cause with a missing-artifact failure. Optional crops must use runtime-derived zero-based half-open bounds verified inside that exact source frame and linked to its digest; generic guidance must not prescribe one fixed crop dimension.

Make compare and baseline-update mutually exclusive explicit run types. A compare run cannot rewrite baselines; an update run writes review candidates separately, preserves prior baselines, and cannot count changed output as a passing comparison.

Manifest each artifact with case ID, role, metadata digest, source relationship, byte size, content digest, comparator identity and policy where relevant. Fail reconciliation on missing, stale, duplicate, or unexpected artifacts.

Use run-scoped staging and ownership-aware cleanup that is safe to repeat after success, assertion failure, render failure, capture failure, comparison failure, timeout, and interruption. A retry must not inherit unmanifested evidence.

Preserve the first causal phase for each case and distinguish readiness or assertion, render, capture, compare, and infrastructure failures; later missing output may be a consequence and must not replace the root phase.

Label non-render assertions, virtual-framebuffer client runs, and interactive-client runs separately. A virtual framebuffer can exercise a client render path in its recorded environment, but it does not prove a physical display, GPU and driver, window manager, native input, accessibility, shader, or full installed-extension-set result.

Verify concrete Fabric Client GameTest, screenshot, readiness, and Loom configuration names against current official Fabric documentation and target-version Fabric API or mappings; keep the rest as workflow guidance rather than a universal API claim.
requiredEvidence: A versioned suite-definition digest, stable expected case-ID set, and per-case semantic metadata
Bounded readiness results and separate expected, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, and not-selected sets

A full-frame artifact for every capture-success, comparison, or visual-pass case; a phase-aware expected-absence record for earlier failures; and bounds-verified, source-bound metadata for any optional crop
An explicit compare or baseline-update run type, immutable baseline and actual digests, comparator metadata, and candidate promotion review
An artifact manifest and reconciliation report covering missing, stale, duplicate, and unexpected output
Idempotent cleanup evidence and per-case causal failure-phase classification
A declared environment class, exact target/runtime metadata, current Fabric documentation evidence, and a bounded statement of what the run proves
guardrails.failureMode: Unstable cases, early screenshots, partial reruns, self-updating baselines, stale files, and unlabeled display environments can produce a green visual suite whose images are neither attributable nor sufficient for its claim.

guardrails.title: Keep Fabric client UI geometry in one resolved scaled coordinate space
rules: Resolve the current scaled viewport once from target-version client screen or window data, then keep layout, drawing, clipping, and hit testing in that coordinate space; do not multiply or divide those coordinates by GUI scale again.

Treat the configured GUI scale as an input to Minecraft's runtime resolution rather than as the layout coordinate system. For Auto, record the resolved scale together with current window, framebuffer, and scaled viewport dimensions instead of treating Auto as one fixed numeric case.

Compute one immutable layout result per viewport and UI state. Draw bounds, local clips, parent clips, effective clips, focus or pointer hit regions, and child placement must all consume that result instead of recomputing related rectangles independently.
Define the effective clip as the intersection of the component clip and every applicable ancestor clip, and keep clip push/pop ownership balanced on every render path.

Measure glyph and image bounds before clipping. Require those pre-clip bounds to fit the intended component, parent, and effective clip, or record an explicit overflow, wrapping, scrolling, ellipsis, or crop policy; a clean post-clip image alone does not prove that content was laid out correctly.

Use the same layout result for hit testing that rendering uses, including normal, hover, pressed, and disabled states; invisible or clipped pixels must not silently leave a larger or shifted interactive region.

Run deterministic geometry assertions for the minimum supported scaled viewport, long localized translations, multiple resolved scale factors, Auto under more than one window size, and normal, hover, pressed, and disabled states.

Pair geometry assertions with actual client rendering or screenshot checks over the same case matrix. Screenshots are visual evidence, not a replacement for numeric bounds, clip intersections, coordinate-space, and hit-test assertions.

Keep this as design and test guidance. Verify exact Screen, window, input, drawing, and scissor API names and behavior against current official Fabric documentation and target-version mappings before generating implementation code.

One captured layout result containing component, content, parent, effective clip, and hit-test bounds for every rendered state
Pre-clip glyph and image measurements plus the declared wrap, scroll, ellipsis, crop, or overflow policy where content does not fit

Deterministic geometry tests covering long localized translations, the minimum supported viewport, multiple resolved scale factors, Auto with multiple window dimensions, and normal, hover, pressed, and disabled states
Actual-render or screenshot evidence for the same matrix, paired with numeric geometry assertions
Current official Fabric custom-screen and GUI-rendering documentation plus target-version mappings for every Minecraft client API named by the implementation
guardrails.failureMode: Applying GUI scale twice or deriving render, clip, and input geometry separately can shrink, offset, clip, or misalign otherwise plausible client UI while screenshot-only checks hide the broken layout contract.

guardrails.title: Bound chunk-spanning world operations and own their lifecycle
rules: Resolve the target Paper version before choosing chunk, scheduler, entity, teleport, block, or event APIs; verify every referenced type, overload, completion context, and lifecycle callback against that version's official Paper Javadocs and documentation.

Convert the complete block, location, or entity selection into a deduplicated set of world-and-chunk coordinates before loading or mutating anything; reject an unbounded or over-limit request before partial world changes begin.

Choose generation policy explicitly for every target chunk and distinguish already generated, allowed to generate, rejected because generation is forbidden, load failure, timeout, and plugin shutdown; do not let a convenience overload choose generation implicitly.

Treat isChunkLoaded as a point-in-time observation, not a lease. If the operation requires a chunk to remain loaded, acquire a plugin-owned chunk ticket through a lifecycle owner that tracks exact coordinates, successful acquisition, sharing or reference counts, and release responsibility.

Do not assume plugin chunk tickets are low-cost or automatically released. Bound the ticket set and lifetime, release only claims owned by the operation, and release or drain every owned claim on complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, unloaded, cancellation, exception, and plugin-disable paths.

Use asynchronous chunk acquisition without waiting or blocking via Future.get or Future.join on a server main, tick, or region thread. API availability and callback or completion context vary by target version, so verify them instead of assuming that an async name implies an arbitrary worker thread.

Async completion proves only that the load request completed; it does not make arbitrary-thread block or entity mutation safe. Transfer each mutation to the target-compatible owning execution context and revalidate the world, chunk, operation generation, and plugin lifecycle there.

Never dereference a retained Chunk, Block, BlockState, mutable Location, or Entity outside its verified owning context. After unload, teleport, region-handoff, or another asynchronous lifecycle change, do not treat it as current until it has been revalidated in its owner. Carry immutable world identity plus coordinates for location work, then re-resolve and validate them in the owning region immediately before use.

On Folia-compatible paths, schedule block and location work on the region that owns that location. Use the entity scheduler as the handoff mechanism for entity work because it follows the entity, then validate the entity's identity, validity, lifecycle state, and operation preconditions inside that owned callback; do not require an unsafe cross-region World.getEntity lookup as the only entity handoff path. A single global main-thread assumption is not a Folia safety model, and separately scheduled regions do not form an atomic multi-region transaction.

Treat an EntityScheduler retired callback as critical code. It must not remove the entity or other entities, load chunks or worlds, or modify ticket levels; record or forward only minimal terminal intent and perform cleanup later in a verified safe execution context.

Apply work in bounded per-tick and per-region batches with explicit item and time budgets, a resumable cursor, cancellation checks, and bounded diagnostics; never process an unbounded chunk, block, or entity selection in one callback.

Represent terminal and resumable results explicitly as complete, partial, rejected, timeout, stale, or unloaded, including attempted, applied, skipped, failed, and remaining counts. A completed Future or callback is not itself proof that every mutation succeeded.

Before each batch and each side effect, recheck preconditions affected by physics, drops, entity movement or removal, teleport, chunk unload, cancellation, and plugin disable. teleportAsync may complete false, and an entity that is unloaded or retired is not thereby proven dead or naturally despawned.

Do not claim that applyPhysics=false makes arbitrary block placement safe; Paper Javadocs warn that it is not generally safe. Model neighboring effects and cross-chunk consequences, and reconcile actual postconditions rather than assuming suppressed physics guarantees persistence.

Make retries and recovery idempotent with operation identity, compare-before-apply checks, per-target progress, and a reconciliation pass that can resume partial work without repeating drops, entity removal, teleports, or other non-idempotent effects.

Treat chunk, entity, teleport, and plugin lifecycle events as race signals that trigger revalidation, not as a complete cleanup or atomicity mechanism. A lifecycle owner must independently reach one terminal state, stop new batches, reconcile committed effects, and release resources exactly once.

tests for loaded and unloaded chunks, generation allowed and denied, chunk boundaries, ticket sharing and release, main-thread wait rejection, stale references, physics and drop side effects, entity movement and removal, teleport false, unload and disable races, partial retry, timeout, Folia ownership boundaries, and idempotent reconciliation
guardrails.failureMode: A chunk-spanning operation can stall a tick thread, generate or pin an unbounded area, mutate from the wrong owner, reuse stale block or entity references, leak tickets, or duplicate partial side effects when loading, unloading, teleportation, physics, and plugin shutdown race its batches.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper custom recipe keys, matching, and reload plugin-owned
rules: Assign every custom recipe a stable NamespacedKey in the owning plugin namespace and retain the exact set of keys that the plugin currently owns.
Parse, normalize, and validate the complete desired definition set before mutating the server recipe registry.
Reconcile only plugin-owned unchanged, added, changed, and removed keys; never use clearRecipes or resetRecipes as plugin reload or disable cleanup.
Treat global recipe-registry replacement as a sequence with partial-failure risk, not an atomic transaction; observe every addRecipe and removeRecipe boolean result.
Publish an explicit applied, rejected, restored, or partial outcome and recover toward the last-known-good owned definitions when replacement fails.
Declare ingredient identity per slot as material-only, exact ItemStack aside from amount, or a separately verified custom flow.
Use RecipeChoice.ExactChoice only when complete ItemStack equality aside from stack size is intended; it is not a subset matcher or an amount constraint.
Do not silently weaken metadata-sensitive ingredients to material-only matching when built-in recipe choices cannot express the product contract.
Validate every key, result, shaped pattern, ingredient symbol, and shapeless count before registry mutation.

Canonicalize shaped recipes from occupied bounds, slot positions, and declared ingredient identity, and shapeless recipes from counted ingredient-identity multisets; include only target-version-verified symmetry behavior.
Reject duplicate keys and report distinct definitions that can match the same crafting input instead of allowing declaration or iteration order to choose an output silently.
Separate recipe-list resends from recipe-book discovery; target-version verify both policies and preserve or remove discovery state only by explicit product decision.
Execute registry mutation in a target-compatible server context and test enable, unchanged reload, add, change, remove, duplicate or conflicting keys, partial failure, disable, and re-enable.
Use a loaded target-version server for registry, matching, consumption, and output claims, plus client evidence when claiming online list visibility or recipe-book behavior.
Expose desired, applied, rejected, restored, and stale keys plus client-resend outcomes without logging sensitive item payloads unnecessarily.
requiredEvidence: a plugin-owned key inventory and desired-versus-applied reconciliation plan
target-version Paper type, member, recipe documentation, and mutation-context evidence
an ingredient-identity matrix with positive and negative matches
canonical match signatures and a collision report for the complete desired set
per-key add and remove results, recovery results, and partial-failure observability

guardrails.failureMode: A recipe reload can delete unrelated recipes, leave a mixed old/new owned set, accept unintended ingredients, lose discovery state, or leave online clients with a stale recipe list.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper display visuals, Interaction targets, and ownership aligned
rules: Resolve the target Paper version and verify every Display subtype, Interaction member, lifecycle member, and event used; type/member indexes do not prove geometry or client behavior.
Define one local-space layout with anchor, axes, units, facing, subtype origin, transformation order, logical rectangles, and offsets, then derive each display and hit-target specification from it.
Treat Display as visual-only and Interaction as the separate hit target; do not infer Interaction bounds from Display width, height, transformation, billboard, view range, or interpolation.
Account for ItemDisplay's centered model origin and BlockDisplay's corner origin, and verify TextDisplay and custom resource-pack model pivots with the target client.
Make the clickable policy explicit during client-side transformation or teleport interpolation; do not assume the server Interaction follows the client's interpolated pose.
Assign stable plugin-owned surface and element IDs, a generation, a display or hit-target role, a persistence policy, and one authoritative registry to every owned entity.

Prepare pending ownership before spawning hit targets, keep every pending Interaction outside live input space, publish only complete registered pairs through one serialized non-suspending transition, and retire the previous generation only after the replacement is authoritative.
Reconcile missing, duplicate, mismatched, and stale owned entities through bounded IDs or indexed locations while preserving malformed or foreign entities for explicit recovery.
Always remove temporary entities explicitly and idempotently; setPersistent(false) and chunk unload are not sufficient cleanup for a never-unloading chunk.
Map an event's current owned Interaction to one logical element, filter the intended hand, define cancellation and eligibility, and execute one terminal action.

Use PlayerInteractEntityEvent for right clicks unless clicked position is specifically required; do not combine it with PlayerInteractAtEntityEvent without handling the documented possible extra delivery.
Keep generic event priority and threading, scheduler ownership, persistent marker schemas, ItemStack identity, and cross-chunk iteration in their dedicated contracts.
Test pure layout math, loaded-server spawn and reconciliation, and real-client rendering and click boundaries separately, and limit claims to the completed evidence layer.
requiredEvidence: target-version Paper type/member/event matches plus official Display, Interaction, and interaction-event behavior documentation
one coordinate and ownership contract that emits paired entity specifications and defines input-unavailable staging, publication, replacement, and rollback
bounded lifecycle and event tests covering pending hit-target exposure, partial spawn, repeated refresh, stale generation, both hands, duplicate delivery, reload, disable, and foreign preservation
target-client visual and input evidence for subtype or custom-model pivots, transformations, billboard behavior, interpolation policy, debug hitboxes, and click boundaries
guardrails.failureMode: An independently positioned visual and hit target can drift, duplicate, execute more than once, leak across lifecycle transitions, or cause broad cleanup to remove another owner's entities.

guardrails.title: Bound Paper persistence and retry whole transactions safely
rules: Build a per-producer matrix of steady and peak rate, burst duration, key cardinality, pending bytes, durability-loss window, visibility latency, ordering, and conflict semantics before choosing a write path.
Prefer a database-side atomic mutation or compare-and-set transition when strict durability, ordering, or preconditions require distinct writes and measured contention is acceptable.
Use per-key delta coalescing only when the domain proves the delta merge associative and commutative, including overflow and range behavior.
Bound pending keys, approximate bytes, oldest age, delta magnitude, concurrent flushes, retry attempts, and total retry time; define a non-blocking admission and durability result at every limit.

Run connection acquisition, statements, commits, rollbacks, retries, and journal I/O outside the Paper server or region tick context, and publish Bukkit-facing results only in a target-compatible context after revalidation.

Flush immutable, stably identified snapshots while new deltas accumulate separately; maintain an invariant that every accepted amount is durable, live pending, explicitly rejected, or in explicit terminal recovery exactly once.

After a known partial result, requeue only the exact uncommitted remainder and merge it atomically with concurrent arrivals; after an unknown commit outcome, reconcile through idempotency, revision, a durable batch ledger, or an adapter-supported outcome check before reapplication.
Retry only serialization or deadlock conflicts identified by documented behavior of the selected database and driver, not by generic exception categories or message text.

A verified retry must roll back and discard the failed transaction, open a fresh transaction, reacquire current state, and rerun the complete unit within bounded attempts, jitter, and an overall deadline.

Keep player-visible, network, command, item-delivery, and other non-idempotent external side effects outside retryable transactions; publish after a known commit or through an idempotent outbox-style boundary.

Close admission before shutdown, stop scheduling, wait behind a bounded in-flight barrier, flush or hand off an explicit undurable remainder, reconcile on restart, and close resources in dependency order.

Observe producer outcomes, pending keys and bytes, oldest age, flush size and latency, retry classification, saturation, ambiguous commits, recovery lag, and shutdown outcome with bounded cardinality and redacted values.

Use controlled clocks, retry-delay sources, executors, barriers, and scripted failures for deterministic races, then verify claimed atomicity, isolation, conflict classification, and retries against the real database adapter and driver.
Route player-connection ownership, generations, reconnect, stale publication, quit, and teardown to paper-player-session-lifecycle instead of duplicating session cleanup rules.
requiredEvidence: An event-rate, durability, visibility, ordering, key-cardinality, and pending-memory matrix for every persistence producer
A per-producer direct-versus-coalesced decision plus proven delta merge laws and configured queue, age, memory, in-flight, and retry bounds
Paper scheduling documentation and tests showing database I/O off the tick context and safe Bukkit-facing publication
Snapshot ownership, exact partial-flush accounting, idempotency or reconciliation, and restart-recovery tests
Official database and driver documentation for retry classification and tests proving fresh whole-transaction retry without repeated external side effects
Deterministic race tests and real-adapter contention tests with adapter, isolation, concurrency, repetitions, invariants, and limitations recorded
A bounded shutdown contract, actionable observability, and explicit routing to paper-player-session-lifecycle for connection cleanup
guardrails.failureMode: An unmeasured or unbounded persistence path can stall ticks, exhaust memory, lose or duplicate partial batches, retry non-retryable failures, repeat side effects, and misstate durability under contention or shutdown.

guardrails.title: Rebuild Paper attribute and effect contributions without claiming foreign state
rules: Derive a complete desired contribution set from authoritative plugin state before mutating ItemMeta, AttributeInstance, or potion effects.
Give every plugin-owned attribute contribution a stable NamespacedKey based on logical source, surface, attribute, and slot grouping where relevant; never generate a fresh identity during reapply.
Keep a bounded registry of current and retired owned attribute keys; do not treat every key in the plugin namespace as owned cleanup scope.
Partition existing modifiers into exact known owned keys and preserved foreign keys, then remove or replace only the owned partition.
Do not rewrite an AttributeInstance base value to represent a session contribution; use the verified transient-modifier contract when the contribution must not persist.
Treat absent ItemMeta modifiers, an explicit empty map, foreign explicit modifiers, and implicit ItemType defaults as distinct states, and prove the effective equipped result.
Do not use attribute-wide, slot-wide, type-wide, or whole-map removal unless an explicit contract owns that entire scope.
Aggregate multiple plugin sources deterministically so retries, reload, and reconnect converge rather than append.
PotionEffectType identifies a collision domain, not a plugin owner; matching effect fields do not establish ownership.
Preserve unexpected active and hidden potion chains by default. Replace or remove a type only while a documented exclusive type lease is valid and observed state still matches it.
Check potion-effect add results and inspect active and hidden chains, including weaker reapply and repeated refresh behavior.
Use bounded effect durations or an explicit recovery contract when a restart can lose the in-memory ownership ledger.
Apply Attribute.MAX_HEALTH and Attribute.MAX_ABSORPTION modifiers before reading capacity and clamping current values; keep zero health at zero and reject non-finite or negative setter inputs.
Reconcile expiry, death, quit, reconnect, reload, disable, and repeated cleanup signals idempotently while preserving vanilla and foreign state.
Keep ItemStack identity, persistent-data schema, scheduler design, and combat-balance values outside this ownership concern.
requiredEvidence: A source, lifetime, surface, stable-key, aggregation, and collision-policy table
Three-way reconciliation tests for desired, existing-owned, and existing-foreign attribute state
Loaded target-version equipment evidence for implicit ItemType defaults and foreign ItemMeta modifiers
Loaded target-version potion evidence for add results, active and hidden chains, weaker reapply, and safe collision handling
Capacity-before-clamp tests for raised and lowered maximum health and absorption, zero health, and invalid numeric inputs
Table-driven lifecycle tests for multiple sources, expiry, death, quit, reconnect, reload, disable, and repeated cleanup
guardrails.failureMode: Anonymous stacking and broad cleanup can outlive a session, delete vanilla or foreign contributions, manufacture ownership for an indistinguishable potion effect, and leave current values invalid after capacity changes.

guardrails.title: Keep Model Engine binding ordered, generation-safe, and evidence-backed
rules: Record the exact Paper build, immutable installed Model Engine plugin and integration artifact identities, supported version pair, hard or soft dependency and load-order policy, and version-matched official API or source evidence before naming external API surfaces.
Use bundled Paper type and member indexes only for Paper carrier and lifecycle surfaces; they do not verify an external Model Engine artifact.

Verify blueprint, model, and animation identifiers with exact case against the selected runtime and exported assets; accept aliases only from an authoritative target-generation mapping and reject missing or ambiguous identifiers.
Distinguish required from optional animations. A missing required animation is an explicit failure, never a silent default, similar-name, normalized-name, or arbitrary substitution.

Declare an already selected carrier as integration-owned or borrowed; snapshot only binding-changed properties for a borrowed carrier, then apply every required target-verified silence, invisibility or other base-entity visibility, and safety property before attachment.

Require a positive attachment result and verify required initial state before publishing the generation. Fail closed when initial attachment fails by withholding publication, detaching partial model state, removing only an integration-owned carrier, and restoring rather than deleting a borrowed carrier. During replacement, retain the last known-good generation or retire all state explicitly; never publish a partial candidate.

Give idle, locomotion, and action channels exactly one logical owner each and document their target-verified priority, masking, loop, interruption, cancellation, natural-end, forced-end, and fallback behavior.
After an action ends or is interrupted, recompute locomotion or idle from current state for the same published generation; reject callbacks from older generations.

Treat Model Engine reload or reimport and any integration reload or disable-enable transition explicitly supported by the target deployment as generation changes; do not assume arbitrary server reload is safe. Use a target-supported coexistence or fail-closed cutover transaction with one publication point, fence old callbacks, then stop and release every old animation owner, active model, adapter reference, registration, and callback.
Follow target Paper completion and entity-ownership rules for teleport before revalidating, resynchronizing, or reattaching through version-matched adapter behavior.

Make despawn and disable cleanup idempotent, bounded, and failure-tolerant; close admission, fence stale callbacks, release model and animation state, remove integration-owned carriers, restore only binding-owned properties on borrowed carriers, and never rely on broad world scans.

Keep dependency absent, unsupported version pair, artifact mismatch, identifier failure, carrier configuration failure, attachment rejection or failure, missing animation, replacement failure, and incomplete cleanup distinct; use a bounded typed plugin outcome when loaded and a declared bootstrap or load-refusal outcome for a hard dependency.
Keep reason-code metrics bounded and separate server-observed binding state from client-observed rendering and carrier visual suppression.

Use deterministic fakes only for the plugin-owned adapter contract. Prove external API compatibility, attachment, animation semantics, reload behavior, and cleanup on the exact loaded artifacts, and prove rendering with a paired target client or captured client state.

Keep combat AI, balance, damage, hitboxes, loot, spawn policy, individual mob or asset authoring, display-interaction geometry and click routing, generic scheduler, event, or persistent-data design, and full Model Engine project validation outside this concern.
requiredEvidence: an exact Paper and Model Engine compatibility row with immutable plugin and adapter artifact identities, dependency and load-order policy, and version-matched official API or source evidence
an exact-case blueprint, model, animation, and alias inventory plus required-versus-optional policy
a carrier ownership and property matrix plus a prepare, attach, verify, publish state machine with fail-closed initial and replacement outcomes
an idle, locomotion, and action ownership and priority matrix with every end and interruption fallback
a generation replacement and idempotent cleanup design for reload or reimport, teleport, despawn, and disable
deterministic adapter tests plus loaded missing-plugin, safely constructible incompatible-version, and controlled attachment-rejection fixtures
exact supported-artifact loaded-server and paired target-client or captured-client evidence
bounded observability proving retired generations, active models, carriers, animation owners, callbacks, and registry entries return to baseline
guardrails.failureMode: An unverified or poorly ordered runtime binding can expose its carrier, attach the wrong asset, silently play a substitute animation, allow channel conflicts, resurrect stale generations, or leave ghost models and carriers after lifecycle transitions.

guardrails.title: Require explicit and complete Paper protection-policy decisions
rules: Resolve the target Paper version and inventory policy actions before choosing listeners. Verify each event and actor, source, cause, affected-target, direction, destination, or proposed-state member against official target-version documentation.
Treat event search results as candidates and record coverage gaps. One plausible event does not prove that direct, indirect, alternate, multi-target, or cross-boundary paths are covered.
Normalize every verified path into actor, source, action, target, cause, boundary, and proposed outcome; do not collapse the policy into target coordinates plus a nullable player.

Keep the immediate source separate from an indirect responsible actor. Resolve a projectile shooter, igniting or priming entity, source block, or other cause only through documented event data or plugin-owned context, and preserve unknown attribution when provenance is absent.

Define an explicit default and conflict precedence for protected, public or unprotected, bypass, vanilla or environmental, plugin-owned, and unknown-cause decisions. A missing matrix row must not silently become allow or deny.

Keep bypass and public access as explicit policy inputs and outcomes rather than scattered listener shortcuts. Reusable guidance must not prescribe a concrete permission name, region geometry, game mode, mob rule, or material list.

Do not equate a null actor with denial or cancel all environmental events inside protected space. Inventory the vanilla mechanics that should remain available and add positive regression cases for them and for ordinary public or unprotected behavior.
Cover multi-event paths independently. An interaction decision does not prove the later placement, ignition, explosion, growth, spread, flow, or entity-change event will be authorized correctly.
Evaluate every affected target and each source-to-target boundary transition. Include outside-to-inside, inside-to-outside, same-policy, different-policy, and mixed multi-target sets.

For pistons, evaluate every moved block and its destination; for explosions, structures, and multi-place actions, evaluate the complete affected set; for flow and spread, evaluate source and destination rather than only the event origin.

Choose whole-event denial or a partial filtered outcome explicitly. Filter affected targets only when the target-version API documents the necessary mutation surface and the policy permits partial application.

Keep the policy function deterministic. Route event priority, prior-cancellation handling, execution context, registration ownership, teardown, and in-flight behavior to the Paper event-listener concern.

Authorize direct plugin-originated world mutations before calling world APIs and route chunk ownership, scheduling, batching, rollback, and shutdown to a separate bounded world-operation lifecycle. Event cancellation is not proof that plugin API mutations are intercepted or atomic.

Use table-driven policy tests for allow and deny, defaults, exceptions, direct and indirect causes, unknown attribution, every boundary direction, and mixed target sets. Include positive preserved-mechanics rows, not only rejection rows.

Use a loaded target-version Paper server for claims about which built-in events fire, which fields the server supplies, and how cancellation or documented filtering affects the world. Constructing built-in events directly is not sufficient runtime evidence because their constructors are not plugin API.
requiredEvidence: an exact target version, official Paper listener documentation, and target-version Javadocs for every event and member used
a behavior-to-event inventory with verified direct, indirect, multi-event, multi-target, and cross-boundary paths plus explicit gaps
an actor, source, action, target, cause, boundary, and outcome matrix with explicit defaults, precedence, and bypass, public, vanilla or environmental, plugin-owned, and unknown-cause decisions
an event-path contract for all affected targets and explicit whole-event or documented partial outcomes
table-driven allow and deny regressions plus loaded-Paper evidence for event wiring and positive preserved-mechanics cases
guardrails.failureMode: A single-coordinate or blanket-cancellation design can miss indirect and cross-boundary changes, apply exceptions inconsistently, break public or vanilla mechanics, and provide false confidence from deny-only tests.

guardrails.title: Keep Paper death settlement and respawn handoff owned and idempotent
rules: Verify the target-version death cancellation, revive-health, item, experience, respawn reason, bed or anchor, post-respawn, location, and nullable world-lookup contracts before implementing the handoff.
Represent VANILLA_DEATH, PLUGIN_OWNED_DOWNED, and RESPAWN_PENDING as mutually exclusive states correlated by a plugin-generated death epoch.

Distinguish plugin cancellation intent from the later non-mutating observed outcome; final isCancelled cannot distinguish uninterrupted ownership from cancel to uncancel to recancel, so require an explicit cancellation-ownership contract such as a cooperative owner token or reviewed exclusive deployment policy and otherwise fail closed without claiming downed state.
Stage or defer downed side effects until cancellation ownership is proven; if an owned effect was provisionally applied, compare-and-roll-back only that exact effect when ownership becomes ambiguous.
Commit one immutable settlement receipt for each uncancelled death epoch and never settle a cancelled downed outcome or replay settlement from a duplicate callback.
Assign each original item exactly one disposition; an item retained through items-to-keep must be removed from drops, and keep-inventory requires a separate explicit drop decision.
Treat keep-level, new experience, new level, new total experience, dropped experience, and should-drop-experience as one coherent settlement rather than independent flags.

Begin destination policy from the server-selected respawn location and preserve it by default; declare explicit precedence before a plugin destination can override bed, respawn anchor, missing-block, or world fallback selection.
Require a finite plugin location whose world resolves and is loaded at decision time; an invalid, unavailable, or denied plugin candidate leaves the original event destination unchanged.
Treat event destination mutation as a decision and record the distinct actual outcome only after the target-verified post-respawn reset boundary.
Consume pending state only for a matching death epoch and target-verified death respawn reason; unrelated portal or plugin respawns must not advance the handoff.
Track every temporary mutation in an ownership ledger and compare-and-restore only exact plugin-owned state, preserving foreign and vanilla changes.

Carry the narrow settlement receipt and destination outcome across quit, reconnect, and reload without retaining live Bukkit objects; disable stops admission, performs bounded owned cleanup, and never starts fire-and-forget recovery.

Test duplicate and out-of-order callbacks, external cancel and uncancel, cancel to uncancel to recancel, competing owners, ambiguous final cancellation, staged side effects, item and experience combinations, invalid and unavailable destinations, bed and anchor precedence, non-death respawns, reconnect, reload, disable, and foreign-state changes.
Keep generic teleport and chunk loading, region protection, complete player-session ownership, combat balance, and game-specific downed or revive mechanics in separate concerns.
requiredEvidence: target-version official Paper or Bukkit documentation for every event and member behavior used
a state-transition table, cancellation-ownership contract, staged-side-effect ledger, item and experience settlement ledger, destination precedence table, and temporary-state ownership ledger
a durable or otherwise reload-safe handoff receipt with distinct destination decision and applied outcome
table-driven deterministic tests plus target-version loaded-server evidence for runtime event and respawn semantics
guardrails.failureMode: Without exclusive ownership, a coherent settlement tuple, preserved vanilla destination precedence, post-respawn outcome observation, and lifecycle reconciliation, death handling can duplicate or erase state and recover into the wrong world or player state.
